question: On a dense joint (q0, omega) grid scored by full-LC Jacobi+surrogate MSE, does the truth-nearest cell rank in a polishable top-K, picking Branch v2 vs v3 for the blind inversion pipeline?
hypothesis: Branch v2: full-LC surrogate scoring puts truth-near cells inside a top-K<=200 polishable set on a 320k joint grid.

artefacts.caption: MSE histogram + top-1000 q-geo x omega-dir scatter, seed 116

narrative_md: Joint (q0, omega) grid pivot on 3 fresh holdout seeds (116/119/103), 320k candidates each: median truth-nearest rank 70823/320000 -- far outside any polishable top-K. Branch v2 (dense grid + top-K polish) is DECISIVELY DEAD: top-50 are ~140-deg-from-truth random LC fitters, no Band A in the grid. The bottleneck axis is the 5-cell LS-bracket |omega| coarseness (20-43% off), not N_dir or N_q. Decision: Branch v3 (multi-anchor consistency) with N_mag densified to 10-15. Surrogate cost realised ~10x the plan estimate (48 ms/candidate). Scoring is blind, but truth-nearest rank reads truth (oracle-leak); N=3 holdout.
